title: Plier-decap a serum bottle: twist off the crimp seal, drop it in the beaker and put the tool down
instruction: Remove the aluminum crimp seal from the serum bottle with the plier decapper, drop the seal in the waste beaker and put the decapper down on the counter. Touch the seal only with the decapper's jaws, and move both hands away at the end.
context: Chromatography and headspace-GC labs, pharma QC and anaerobic-culture labs close vials and serum bottles with 20 mm aluminum crimp seals and remove them with a hand decapper to re-sample, empty or recycle the glass. WHEATON's guide for its 224373 plier decapper: "secure the seal between the jaws, squeeze the handles and twist the seal". O*NET 19-4031.00 Chemical Technicians, core task: "Set up and conduct chemical experiments, tests, and analyses, using techniques such as chromatography ..."
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left); heights above the counter. Lab preparation counter (the table) with a white reagent shelf at the back (800 wide, 420 tall, front at x 495). WHEATON 223747 100 mL clear glass serum bottle (52 diameter, 95 tall with its seal; 110 g, an estimate), empty, standing at x 290, y 50, closed with a grey W224100-405 stopper under a WHEATON 224178-01 20 mm open-top aluminum seal crimped over the 20 mm finish (seal 21.5 outside, 7.6 tall, 13 mm centre hole, about 1 g: estimates). WHEATON 224373 plier decapper (steel, grey plastic-coated handles; 157 long, 160 g, estimates) lying flat on its handles, jaws pointing +y, rivet at x 250, y -120, its jaws open 0.55 rad from closed on the seal (jaw tips 32 apart; fixture/dimensions.svg). PYREX 1000-250 250 mL low-form glass beaker (68 outside x 90; 110 g, an estimate), empty, at x 370, y -45. Lot B: bottle at x 270, y 80 and beaker at x 365, y -15; the plier as in lot A. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A. Lower-cost real trial: the same 224373 plier, ALK/Allergy Labs SV10020SILVER-25 empty pre-sealed 100 mL bottles (25-pack), the same beaker and a 10x loupe: $320.76 before tax/shipping, priced in README. This is a named substitute closure, not a WHEATON torque calibration. Admit only bottles with 20 mm finish, 52 +/-1 mm diameter and 95 +/-1 mm sealed height; inspect the glass and reject a seal that turns by hand. The supplier does not publish the substitute bottle dimensions; these are enrolment checks. A reusable-bottle route with named Kebby 20001-00-C05A crimper is $474.51.
scoring: Read from the overhead video and a side camera level with the seal, stepped frame by frame, close photos of the bottle neck against a 1 mm rule, and a 10x loupe. Score 0 for the whole trial if, at any moment, a robot finger touches the aluminum seal (simulation: over 0.5 N), the plier chips or cracks the glass (loupe; simulation: over 20 N of plier-on-glass contact), or the bottle or beaker falls over (tilts past 45 degrees). Every score needs, for the last 1 s, the bottle standing (tilted 10 degrees or less, base within 3 mm of the counter) and the bottle, seal, beaker and plier still. 1.0: the seal lies inside the waste beaker below its rim, the plier lies on the counter (lowest point within 4 mm of it, tilted 15 degrees or less), and both hands have been at least 30 mm from all four for 1 s. 0.75: seal in the beaker; the plier not put down or the hands not clear. 0.5: the seal off the bottle, no part of it within 10 mm of the glass or stopper (simulation: an 11.5 mm sphere round its centre), but not in the beaker. 0.25: the crimp is torn (the seal is loose and turns on the neck; simulation: it has accumulated 90 degrees of credited relative twist beyond the crimp's 0.1 rad credited-slip deadband (native stiffness 5 N m/rad, force cap at 0.05 rad), with a configured 0.25 N m torque cap, while both jaws pressed it with 25 N or more) but the seal is still on or near the bottle. 0 otherwise. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged.
run_limit: 2,400 steps (120 s at 20 Hz) per trial; two trials (lots A and B)
reset_notes: Use a new seal every trial. WHEATON route: inspect an empty 223747 bottle under a 10x loupe and reject any chip; fit W224100-405 stopper and crimp a new 224178-01 seal with a 20 mm crimper at one recorded setting. Reject a seal that turns by hand. Lower-cost ready-sealed route: take a fresh ALK/Allergy Labs SV10020SILVER-25 bottle; verify 20 mm finish, 52 +/-1 mm diameter, 95 +/-1 mm overall sealed height, intact glass, grey stopper and silver seal that does not turn by hand. Reject mismatches. The supplier gives no outside dimensions, so measure the actual lot. Record the specimen product and torque check; no physical calibration is claimed. Empty the waste beaker. Place bottle and beaker on the selected lot tape outlines; lay plier flat on its outline, jaws open 0.55 rad from closed (jaw tips 32 mm apart; fixture/dimensions.svg). Arms start at their default pose. Recycle the torn seal. Allow about a minute for ready-sealed specimen inspection and placement (setup estimate); reusable bottles need a new seal crimped at the recorded setting.
fidelity: Native seal-bottle joint: 0.25 N m torque estimate (0.6 x assumed 50 N x 8.3 mm; Mathaes RSF range 7-115 N). Native stiffness 5 N m/rad; credited slip beyond 0.1 rad, tear at 90 deg. Grip >=25 N/jaw: Coulomb bound 23.3 N rounded up. Glass >20 N stress proxy (25 MPa x assumed 0.8 mm2), not chip calibration. Pin friction 0.48 N m estimated; no spring/viscous drive. Other geometry/masses estimated; solid 32-sided seal collider.
scores: Scripted demo demo-20261124T070902: mean 0.375 over lots A and B (not full score). The Dream-1 video shown is from the earlier source (dream-20261121T105312); Dream-1 on this source had not finished at push time.
